Requirement: Each controller shall preserve its allocated autonomous function during host or network unavailability.
Acceptance: For every allocated autonomous function, verify approved physical host/link outage and reconnection where such links exist; local function remains within its allocated behavior and remote status reports unavailable. For standalone targets with no external link, demonstrate independent cold start and operation; absent links are recorded as not present, not passed HIL cases.

Requirement: Each physical resource shall have one designated owner or approved explicit arbitration, including DMA and shared peripherals.
Acceptance: Manifest and resource assignment review resolve all owners and arbitration.

Requirement: Remote clients shall submit typed intent rather than direct hardware operations.
Acceptance: Review every exposed operation against the approved semantic contract catalog. In the benign reference, demonstrate that only typed operations reach the local owner and that unsupported raw-device operations cannot be admitted. Authorization follows ASR-004; local authority follows SYS-002.

Requirement: Where physical feedback is allocated, observed state shall report the measured value and its validity independently of the requested or commanded state.
Acceptance: Use a benign bench with independently measured feedback and known requested/actual disagreement, delayed feedback and unavailable sensor cases. The observation matches the measurement within the allocated tolerance and quality policy; simulated results are separately labeled.

Requirement: Vehicle, physical, VM and service lifecycle ownership shall remain distinct.
Acceptance: Authority matrix covers independent states and transition owners.

Requirement: A controller shall refuse readiness when mandatory capabilities, dependency checks or configuration admission fail.
Acceptance: Missing capability and invalid configuration fixtures prevent readiness.

Requirement: Resource authority shall be allocated through reset, boot, maintenance and shutdown.
Acceptance: Ownership and startup-state matrix approved; no gap or competing owner.

Requirement: Multiple authorized requesters shall have explicit precedence/arbitration and conflict policy.
Acceptance: Conflicting intent fixture produces approved result without implicit last-writer authority.

Requirement: Delegated DSP, GPU, NPU or specialized control accelerators shall have allocated authority, resource budgets and unavailable-state semantics.
Acceptance: Ownership and bounded workload evidence show independent local functions remain within allocations.

Requirement: Each release shall define a minimal mandatory core and a build-time feature dependency graph; disabled optional capabilities shall not contribute their exclusive runtime code or data to the embedded image.
Acceptance: Build admitted feature-on and feature-off configurations, including AI. Map and binary inspection find no exclusive disabled-feature runtime symbols or model data, and applicable core regressions pass.

Requirement: Each reusable application component shall have a versioned placement-independent descriptor defining identity, release, typed ports, runnable triggers, execution and resource allocations, lifecycle, dependencies, criticality, failure disposition, state schema and accountable maintainer.
Acceptance: Build a standalone and two-component composition from the same schema. Replace one component with an independently authored conforming implementation without modifying unrelated component or generic core source; reject duplicate identity, unresolved dependency, incompatible port, invalid trigger and missing allocation. Isolation assessed under RT-026.

Requirement: A relocatable application component shall be deployable in admitted local and remote placements without changes to its domain algorithm source, subject to approved timing, resource and authority allocation.
Acceptance: Build the same benign component source in a standalone controller, a local consolidated composition and a distributed placement; compare typed semantic outputs and timing within predeclared tolerances. Source diff excludes domain algorithm edits. Reject incompatible placement; link loss respects SYS-001.

Requirement: Each selected zonal deployment shall have a machine-readable topology allocating physical I/O, power domains, wake dependencies and communication routes.
Acceptance: Validate topology against reviewed bench wiring; reject duplicate exclusive ownership, missing mandatory endpoints and contradictory routes. Resource authority follows SYS-002.

Requirement: A selected redundant deployment shall define single-owner failover authority, synchronization assumptions and state validity under peer loss, partition and restart.
Acceptance: Independent analysis and benign physical bench verify single authorized owner or approved non-actuating state across peer loss, partial communication and restart; synchronization and degraded state meet allocated bounds.

Requirement: Each typed application port shall declare interaction type, initial validity, delivery, lifetime and version-evolution semantics independently of transport.
Acceptance: Local and remote fixtures cover initial validity, repeated events or coalescing, correlation, expiry, producer restart and supported old/new consumers. Incompatible versions refused or explicitly adapted without silent semantic change; unsupported mappings fail composition; authority follows SYS-002/003.

Requirement: Embedded execution shall use native Zephyr kernel and driver APIs; portable domain logic shall remain independent of RTOS and vendor APIs. A generic capability shall not be reimplemented when an admitted maintained native or upstream implementation meets the allocation.
Acceptance: Dependency audit and minimal build show no mandatory parallel RTOS, duplicate generic scheduler, driver, storage framework or hardware facade. Each exception records a capability gap, rejected alternatives and maintenance owner.

Requirement: Every runnable context, including interrupts, vendor threads and callbacks, shall declare trigger or period, deadline, priority, resource and blocking bounds.
Acceptance: Reconcile all runnable contexts with the resolved build/runtime inventory under RT-019; each entry has an owner, trigger or period, deadline, priority, resource and blocking allocation with units or approved inapplicability. No context without an approved allocation enters the admitted configuration.

Requirement: ISR work shall be bounded and not block on remote or persistence work.
Acceptance: Reviewed ISR path and measured bound within approved allocation.

Requirement: Local RT execution shall not await host transport.
Acceptance: Local timing remains within allocated bound during host outage.

Requirement: Critical-path resource allocation shall be static or demonstrably bounded.
Acceptance: Inspect allocation sites and configured bounds; exercise exactly-at-limit and one-over-limit requests. Exhaustion returns the defined result without corrupting state.

Requirement: Each device shall have explicit state writer and snapshot ownership.
Acceptance: Single approved writer and coherent versioned snapshots.

Requirement: Shared locks shall have a declared acquisition order and bounded hold time, including allocated priority-inversion controls.
Acceptance: Review all lock acquisition paths; no remote or I/O wait under a shared state lock. Under approved contention, measured hold and blocking times meet target allocations.

Requirement: Periodic tasks shall track release and deadline using a monotonic time base with declared counter-wrap handling.
Acceptance: Test release drift, late cycles, time-base wrap and wall-clock adjustment. No unapproved duplicate release or deadline reset; late-cycle disposition matches policy.

Requirement: Target timing analysis shall account for interrupt, DMA, cache, bus, flash, memory, clock and frequency-transition interference within the allocated operating modes.
Acceptance: Approved analysis and measurements cover worst allocated conditions; observed maxima are not WCET proof.

Requirement: G1 benign local task shall meet provisional 10 ms deadline.
Acceptance: On the approved G1-C-LAB physical workload, independently timestamp every release and completion for 24 h. Zero observed misses of the 10 ms deadline; publish sample count and timing uncertainty, and separately accept response-time analysis. This is not a WCET proof.

Requirement: Nominal request acceptance/refusal shall meet provisional 100 ms target.
Acceptance: Freeze the nominal UART request types, rate, concurrency and timestamp boundaries before test; every admitted or refused request in the measured nominal workload completes its acceptance/refusal response within 100 ms, including stated measurement uncertainty. Report sample count and maximum.

Requirement: Lab flash and RAM headroom shall be at least 20 percent.
Acceptance: For the approved G1-C-LAB target, separately compute (available budget minus used bytes) / available budget for flash and RAM; both are at least 20%. Include reserved sections, maximum allocated stack and pool use; record linker map, runtime high-water observations and analysis assumptions.

Requirement: Nominal queues shall remain below 80 percent occupancy.
Acceptance: For each allocated nominal queue in the approved G1-C-LAB workload, record high-water occupancy divided by configured usable capacity. Each ratio is strictly below 0.80; test saturation separately under RT-005 and report its specified disposition.

Requirement: Bulk work shall not consume reserved core capacity.
Acceptance: Core requests accepted within allocation under bulk load.

Requirement: Health shall distinguish alive, deadline and logical supervision.
Acceptance: Missing or invalid required progress produces defined degraded report.

Requirement: Watchdog servicing shall follow approved progress policy and explicit ownership of each internal or external watchdog.
Acceptance: Loss of required progress produces allocated reaction; independent supervision where required; no unconditional feed.

Requirement: Critical event paths shall not rely on work submission as occurrence counting.
Acceptance: Repeated events accounted for or explicit overflow reported; no lost required item.

Requirement: Selected zbus channels shall have analyzed observer context, notification and wait bounds.
Acceptance: Observer types, timeout, resource budget and measured path documented.

Requirement: Target integration shall reconcile the actual runnable contexts of the resolved kernel and vendor build against the RT-002 inventory.
Acceptance: Build and runtime inventory comparison identifies no unallocated context.

Requirement: Work buffer lifetime shall extend through completion or synchronized cancellation.
Acceptance: Ownership fixtures cover pending and canceled work; no premature reuse.

Requirement: Runtime and system power management, including approved frequency and clock transitions, shall preserve allocated local deadlines, time quality, peripheral availability and device ownership.
Acceptance: On each admitted physical power/frequency mode and transition, verify native driver capabilities, balanced references, wake latency, timestamp validity and deadlines against allocation. Incompatible modes are rejected or disabled.

Requirement: Selected SMP or AMP execution shall use an approved core and interrupt allocation with bounded inter-core communication and analyzed shared-resource interference.
Acceptance: Review affinity, interrupt routing, mailbox behavior, cache/interconnect contention and cross-core synchronization budgets; physical stress and response-time analysis meet allocation or exclude the configuration.

Requirement: DMA and shared-memory ownership shall follow target coherency, alignment, barriers and buffer lifetime requirements.
Acceptance: Independent benign producer/consumer fixtures validate transfer integrity and completion/cancellation behavior.

Requirement: Hardware-triggered acquisition and output scheduling shall preserve declared timing accuracy and report event age, sequence, uncertainty and overrun status where allocated.
Acceptance: External timestamp measurements meet allocated accuracy, synchronization and jitter including clock transitions; missed trigger and full-buffer fixtures report overrun, never silently lose required events.

Requirement: Portable numeric algorithms shall declare precision, overflow, rounding and floating-point context assumptions.
Acceptance: Golden boundary vectors pass on selected compiler and CPU configurations.

Requirement: Each selected consolidated application shall have enforceable CPU, stack, heap, static-memory, queue and I/O allocations appropriate to its isolation domain.
Acceptance: Map and runtime watermarks attribute enforceable CPU, stack, heap, static-memory, queue and I/O budgets to each application or explicitly shared isolation domain. Exercise each allocated limit and one-over-limit case; other functions meet deadlines; unsupported enforcement fails admission.

Requirement: Accelerator job admission and execution shall be bounded by declared job, buffer, completion and concurrency limits.
Acceptance: Queue-limit, timeout, unavailable-provider and reset fixtures report the defined job outcome; independent deterministic tasks stay within allocation. Authority allocation follows SYS-009 and AI fallback follows ADOPT-054.

Requirement: Profiling instrumentation shall be independently selectable and its timing and memory overhead quantified for the reference configuration.
Acceptance: Compare builds with tracing enabled and disabled; report timing, CPU, RAM, flash and collection bandwidth overhead under declared workloads. Reject evidence from incompatible instrumented images.

Requirement: Each allocated time-critical runnable context shall have a defined deadline-miss disposition.
Acceptance: Trace every time-critical context in RT-002 to its specified reaction; controlled late-release and overrun fixtures demonstrate detection and allocated response within its approved bound. If no context is time-critical, document the allocation and rationale; physical timing evidence is required for physical claims.

Requirement: Each target shall have an immutable composition manifest identifying ISA, core/revision, execution mode, memory map, board, configuration, toolchain, capabilities, allocated resources, resolved component identities and evidence.
Acceptance: Manifest records exact resolved hardware and build inputs; correlate component descriptors and native configuration with explicit absent capabilities. Deployment reconciliation follows PL-024.

Requirement: Generic services shall not depend on product or vendor-private headers; target-specific implementation shall remain in native BSP or thin domain adapters.
Acceptance: Dependency gate passes on two selected targets; new device provider requires no generic core edit.

Requirement: Build-time composition shall reject unresolved feature dependencies, unsupported execution modes and conflicting hardware resources.
Acceptance: Invalid feature/core/resource combinations fail before deployment, including contradictory or unknown capability predicates and mandatory dependency omission. Applicability resolution is verified under VER-023.

Requirement: Physical wiring shall use native board/device configuration and approved driver bindings, with explicit pinmux and resource assignment.
Acceptance: Resolved DTS/pinctrl and ownership match reviewed schematic and hardware facts.

Requirement: Product policy shall be independently configurable from board wiring.
Acceptance: Second product policy does not modify generic implementation.

Requirement: The reference portfolio shall execute a common benign application on physical MCU targets from at least two independent vendors without changes to generic core or domain algorithm source.
Acceptance: Independent physical conformance reports use a common versioned application and core source, with source diffs confined to admitted target configuration, native BSP or provider integration. Record engineering hours, measured behavior, limitations and ISA coverage; an additional ISA is evaluated when an eligible physical port exists, otherwise its evidence remains open. Simulation cannot satisfy the two-vendor physical criterion.

Requirement: Target admission shall declare unsupported capabilities and classify native execution, isolated integrated execution or external interoperability; unsupported native ports shall not be advertised.
Acceptance: Manifest distinguishes integration paths; required unavailable capability blocks admission.

Requirement: Released target shall bind source, config, toolchain and image identity.
Acceptance: Build metadata fully reconstructs approved inputs.

Requirement: Configuration conflicts among product, Kconfig and devicetree shall fail admission.
Acceptance: Contradictory fixture rejected; manifest records actual resolved values.

Requirement: The authoritative target maturity record shall distinguish candidate, software-implemented, simulated, physically validated and independently qualified capability states for the exact board, revision, profile, transport, OS and toolchain configuration.
Acceptance: For each exact target and capability, publish separately attributable software, simulation, physical validation and independent qualification verdicts, evidence references and open gaps. An unavailable or failed gate cannot be represented as passed; a qualified subset cannot promote a different board, build, driver or application. Public output is generated under ADOPT-043.

Requirement: Public interfaces shall declare semantic API compatibility and applicable ABI, endianness, alignment, width, ownership and serialization constraints, including selected foreign-language bindings without requiring a second core runtime.
Acceptance: Cross-target golden vectors and supported compiler/ABI checks pass. For selected C++ or Rust bindings, verify layout, error and ownership behavior. No raw-structure wire ABI assumption.

Requirement: ZARC shall admit native targets only with a maintained or explicitly owned Zephyr port, compatible toolchain, approved vendor SDK access and documented architecture support.
Acceptance: Port owner, licensing, supported ISA/toolchain, boot and representative native build evidence recorded; otherwise external integration only.

Requirement: Target memory placement shall respect TCM, cacheability, executable regions, MPU/MMU and external-memory initialization, integrity, availability, endurance and bandwidth constraints where applicable.
Acceptance: Linker map and native configuration demonstrate approved placement and initialization dependencies; physical startup and bounded memory behavior meet allocated constraints when external memory is selected.

Requirement: Selected lockstep or split-lock operating mode shall be explicitly configured and matched to vendor assumptions and firmware topology.
Acceptance: Mode evidence and approved vendor diagnostic status demonstrate correct admitted configuration.

Requirement: Accelerator integration shall use versioned native or vendor provider contracts with explicit supported operations, precision, alignment, memory and timeout capabilities.
Acceptance: Provider capability tests compare supported CPU and accelerator results within approved tolerances; unsupported operations fail clearly.

Requirement: Targets shall declare privilege separation, MPU/MMU regions and DMA protection capability; configurations requiring unavailable protection shall fail admission.
Acceptance: Build fixtures reject unprotected layouts; physical benign isolation test and review confirm allocated region boundaries.

Requirement: Virtual device providers shall preserve the native application-facing contracts and identify simulated data at the boundary.
Acceptance: Same benign application builds against physical-provider and virtual-provider configurations without generic source changes; virtual reports carry simulation provenance and production build excludes unapproved virtual providers.

Requirement: Each selected service shall publish a versioned descriptor with stable ID, dependencies, readiness, lifecycle, budget and access classification.
Acceptance: Registry is complete and unique; compare resolved service manifest to authorized catalog; unavailable, stopped and degraded services distinguishable. Missing mandatory service blocks readiness under SYS-006.

Requirement: Composition shall reject cycles or missing mandatory dependencies.
Acceptance: Invalid dependency fixtures fail admission.

Requirement: Startup shall publish readiness only after allocated hardware initialization, boot dependencies and required service checks succeed.
Acceptance: For each admitted mandatory hardware and service dependency, execute successful, failed and delayed initialization fixtures. Readiness is published only after all required checks succeed; dependent functions remain explicitly unavailable otherwise.

Requirement: Failed initialization shall release initialized resources in defined order.
Acceptance: Rollback fixture confirms resource disposition.

Requirement: Quiesce shall reject new work except explicit allowed scope.
Acceptance: Approved state transitions and request results observed.

Requirement: Resume from suspend shall revalidate dependencies and feedback; stopped services shall reinitialize before readiness.
Acceptance: Suspend/resume and stop/start fixtures prove distinct paths.

Requirement: Reset shall invalidate prior session assumptions and assess reset cause and retained-state validity before reuse.
Acceptance: Old epoch rejected; retained-state validity and fresh snapshot verified on selected reset modes.

Requirement: Diagnostic records shall identify source, epoch, monotonic timestamp, quality, schema version, allocated correlation identity and build/configuration identity.
Acceptance: Golden records validate fields and correlation across a benign multi-service scenario; missing clock synchronization explicit; protected data excluded. Distributed correlation follows CON-032.

Requirement: Logs, stored faults, telemetry and trace collection shall enforce allocated retention, priority, sampling and resource limits without blocking critical execution.
Acceptance: Under normal and overload workloads, retention and drop counters reconcile with observed records, reserved resources remain available, and allocated control timing is preserved.

Requirement: Each selected persistent block shall define consistency, schema version, defaults, integrity, storage-specific atomicity, retention, endurance and read/write completion policy, including redundancy where allocated.
Acceptance: Corrupt, interrupted, capacity-limit and reset fixtures produce specified validity or recovery. Each supported schema transition verifies migration, unsupported-transition refusal and recovery; endurance analysis and physical interruption evidence for selected storage.

Requirement: Every service transition shall declare preconditions, deadline and failure disposition.
Acceptance: Review each allocated lifecycle transition for preconditions, deadline and defined failure disposition. Exercise valid, disallowed and deadline-expired transitions; verify resulting state and bounded completion against the approved transition table.

Requirement: Cancellation shall distinguish request cancellation from observed physical effect.
Acceptance: In-flight cancellation does not fabricate reversed/completed state.

Requirement: Failure of an application or service shall not disable an independent allocated function unless an approved dependency requires the specified degradation.
Acceptance: In an admitted benign isolation fixture, component timeout, resource exhaustion and restart preserve independent function within budget or report allocated degradation. Hardware isolation claims require physical evidence.

Requirement: Selected engineering measurement and calibration interfaces including XCP/A2L shall expose only approved typed data and calibration operations through allocated authority.
Acceptance: Approved independent engineering client passes scoped read and calibration fixtures; configuration policy preserved.

Requirement: The selected diagnostic event manager shall represent configured event-to-diagnostic-code mappings, event status, qualification/debounce, occurrence counters, aging and allocated freeze-frame data under product policy.
Acceptance: Golden event sequences verify code mapping, threshold transitions, aging, counter saturation, freeze-frame association and reset retention; unavailable persistence or unmapped codes are reported according to the configured policy. Diagnostic protocol exposure is separately verified under ADOPT-017.

Requirement: Diagnostic sessions and operations shall declare state preconditions, authorization, timeout, response semantics and resource limits.
Acceptance: Independent benign diagnostic client verifies allowed and refused requests, session expiration and simultaneous client limits.

Requirement: A selected vehicle-mode policy shall coordinate application availability, network modes, wake sources and shutdown dependencies without conflating independent host and controller lifecycle states.
Acceptance: State-transition matrix covers normal, sleep, wake, service and degraded modes and independent host restart; denied or incompatible transitions leave state unchanged.

Requirement: A selected network-management provider shall coordinate communication availability and sleep/wake under explicit per-network policy, including selective wake and bounded wake-event handling where allocated.
Acceptance: Independent peer verifies mode transitions, repeated wake events, simultaneous wake reasons and network loss; local autonomy and power allocations remain valid.

Requirement: Signal transformation shall preserve type, scale, units, timestamp, quality and unavailable-state semantics across conversion boundaries.
Acceptance: Golden vectors cover signed ranges, saturation, rounding, unavailable and invalid values; independent peer agrees on results.

Requirement: Power-domain sequencing shall define dependencies, feedback validity, inrush constraints and allocated fallback under interrupted transitions.
Acceptance: Low-voltage benign bench validates approved sequences, feedback loss and independent protection behavior; no production electrical claim from simulation.

Requirement: The selected diagnostic event manager shall apply the configured event enable and storage conditions without altering underlying measured fault quality.
Acceptance: Test enabled/disabled transitions and event qualification boundaries; disabled storage does not fabricate healthy status or erase independently required evidence.

Requirement: A selected diagnostic function-availability policy shall determine the availability of an allocated benign function from configured event states and approved inhibit conditions.
Acceptance: Golden event combinations, stale event and unknown state produce specified availability; inhibited function cannot be represented as available, and independent functions are unaffected.

Requirement: A selected power-loss notification interface shall initiate only the product-allocated bounded shutdown or persistence disposition before power becomes unavailable.
Acceptance: On an approved low-voltage fixture, verify time available, defined state outcome and bounded work at minimum allocated hold-up; missing notification is handled under the storage recovery contract.

Requirement: Each external operation shall have a versioned semantic contract defining its type, unit, authorized role, bounds, response and physical-effect semantics.
Acceptance: Contract schema includes all mandatory fields; valid, invalid and incompatible-version golden fixtures meet the contract. External contracts do not confer raw hardware authority (SYS-003).

Requirement: Every physical link shall own independent session state.
Acceptance: Two simulated links reset independently without shared stale state.

Requirement: Incompatible major contract shall block writes.
Acceptance: Mismatch fixtures return incompatible and no state change.

Requirement: Unknown mandatory values shall be refused.
Acceptance: Invalid enum/required-field fixtures fail deterministically.

Requirement: Requests shall have bounded validity; expiry shall prevent admission outside approved validity window.
Acceptance: Expired request refused without effect; retention governed by CON-016.

Requirement: Duplicate desired-state requests shall preserve consistent outcome within scoped retention; ID reuse with different intent shall be refused.
Acceptance: Same session/principal/method/ID fixture matches retained outcome; changed payload refused.

Requirement: Acknowledgment shall be distinct from feedback-confirmed completion.
Acceptance: Event fixture reports actual outcome independently of acceptance.

Requirement: Timeout shall report unknown outcome where confirmation absent.
Acceptance: Client reconciles snapshot rather than declaring false failure.

Requirement: Observations shall carry quality, producer boot epoch and generation; link session identity shall remain separate.
Acceptance: Host stale and restarted producer/peer fixtures preserve boot/session distinction.

Requirement: Provider shall expose bounded send/receive, readiness and lifecycle.
Acceptance: Provider conformance passes declared capabilities.

Requirement: UART companion link shall preserve semantic contract.
Acceptance: Golden fixtures pass approved UART target configuration.

Requirement: A lost link shall invalidate its remote observations and pending link assumptions without revoking allocated local authority.
Acceptance: Independent link loss reports unavailable and reconciles upon return; local autonomy verified under SYS-001.

Requirement: Transport budget shall include line capacity, processing and queue overhead.
Acceptance: Measured latency and utilization documented against budget.

Requirement: The transport freshness contract shall distinguish producer and receiver clock identity, synchronization epoch, transit age, uncertainty and validity.
Acceptance: Test independent clock drift, restart, unknown synchronization and stale samples; observations are refused or marked as required, with no false freshness claim.

Requirement: Snapshot/event handover shall detect gaps and reconcile generations.
Acceptance: Event during snapshot and missing-event cases recover without stale valid claim.

Requirement: Outstanding work and retained results shall have explicit capacity, retention and eviction semantics.
Acceptance: Exhaustion returns BUSY; evicted outcomes reported unknown; bounded cache under stress.

Requirement: Target UART peripheral shall use one selected API with exclusive ownership and separate console.
Acceptance: Native driver supports chosen API; no conflicting callbacks; buffer lifecycle and recovery verified.

Requirement: Transport provider shall publish ordering, delivery, sizing, backpressure and failure mapping.
Acceptance: Provider capability/mapping conformance available for each selected binding.

Requirement: Selected CAN diagnostic transport shall support the admitted ISO-TP profile including segmentation, flow-control limits, timeouts and explicit delivery failures.
Acceptance: Independent ISO-TP peer exchanges benign short and segmented payloads; boundary size, timeout and capacity tests pass.

Requirement: Selected DoIP binding shall preserve approved diagnostic authority, connection lifecycle, routing activation policy and bounded resource use.
Acceptance: Independent compliant peer validates admitted discovery and diagnostic exchange, inactive routing and connection-limit handling.

Requirement: Selected SOME/IP discovery shall expose versioned service instances, availability, subscription lifetimes and restart semantics.
Acceptance: Independent peer tests service appearance, withdrawal, expiry, version mismatch and recovery without stale availability.

Requirement: Signal and service routing shall use generated, versioned mappings with explicit conversion, freshness, authority and drop policy.
Acceptance: Golden multi-network fixtures cover mapping mismatch, unavailable signals, overload and independent endpoint restart.

Requirement: Wire decoding shall enforce the schema-defined maximum encoded size, collection length and nesting depth before allocating resources or admitting an operation.
Acceptance: Valid maximum-size fixture decodes; size/depth/count one-over-limit and malformed fixtures are refused without state mutation or excess resource use. Unknown mandatory fields follow CON-004.

Requirement: A selected non-automotive interoperability binding shall use an independently versioned adapter with an admitted profile and authority contract, without expanding the mandatory automotive core.
Acceptance: For each advertised adapter (for example an allocated CANopen, industrial data or ROS 2/micro-ROS integration), record pinned protocol/version, native versus host placement and declared operations. An independent compatible peer passes normal, unavailable and version-mismatch fixtures with no mandatory core change. No unselected sector protocol is implied.

Requirement: A selected grouped-signal contract shall publish a coherent generation of all mandatory group members or mark the group incomplete.
Acceptance: Boundary fixtures cover concurrent producer updates, missing member, old generation and complete group; consumers never accept a mixed generation as valid.

Requirement: A selected safety-related communication path shall implement the allocated end-to-end data protection behavior using an approved provider and contract.
Acceptance: Approved independent benign fixtures verify expected integrity, sequence and freshness outcomes; safety residual-error analysis and accepted assumptions remain ASR-010. No safety claim from software test alone.

Requirement: A selected cyclic signal exchange shall apply its configured transmission period, receive deadline and unavailable-state policy.
Acceptance: Nominal, boundary and missed-period fixtures demonstrate transmission timing and timeout quality within allocated uncertainty; stale data is not represented as current.

Requirement: Each selected packed legacy signal binding shall implement its approved frame-to-signal encoding and decoding contract, independently of internal typed application representation.
Acceptance: Independent golden vectors cover selected frame ID, length, bit position/order, signedness, scaling, multiplexer where applicable, invalid encoding and numeric boundaries; decoded values match the approved contract. Incompatible mappings are rejected; timing is verified under CON-030 and semantic transformations under SVC-021.

Requirement: In a broker-mediated topology, the trusted broker shall own the physical host link exclusively.
Acceptance: Approved guest clients mediate through broker; no competing direct host link.

Requirement: Host shall clear validity and outstanding assumptions after restart.
Acceptance: New session and fresh snapshot required.

Requirement: Broker shall enforce quotas and reserved capacity.
Acceptance: Agreed benign client load preserves core admission.

Requirement: VHAL mapping shall preserve approved property and power semantics.
Acceptance: Pinned AAOS property fixtures cover readiness and unavailable status.

Requirement: SDV mapping shall distinguish service and physical readiness.
Acceptance: Service startup/outage fixtures report correct status.

Requirement: A selected host SOME/IP integration shall use approved service, method, event, instance and version identifiers with the admitted host binding.
Acceptance: An independent peer verifies the pinned method, event and version fixtures; CommonAPI conformance is tested when selected. Discovery/subscription behavior is separately verified under CON-021. No CommonAPI dependency is mandatory on a resource-constrained controller.

Requirement: Guest lifecycle shall remain independent of physical state.
Acceptance: Guest restart does not cause unapproved transition.

Requirement: Shutdown readiness shall aggregate required guests with bounded coordination.
Acceptance: Missing readiness follows approved fallback status.

Requirement: VHAL power request and report directions and state-dependent parameters shall match pinned AOSP branch.
Acceptance: Property direction, state values, cancel and postpone fixtures pass.

Requirement: The broker shall enforce reviewed identity delegation from authenticated principals to scoped service authority.
Acceptance: Independent review and contract tests verify principal-to-capability mapping.

Requirement: Hypervisor configuration shall have actual resource assignment and isolation evidence.
Acceptance: VM/physical device access, reset and failure-domain assumptions reviewed.

Requirement: High-performance host adapters shall be independently replaceable without changing the generic controller application or its authority boundary.
Acceptance: Integrate two selected host reference configurations with the same controller binary and semantic fixtures; document adapter differences.

Requirement: Integrated host and guest configurations shall define independent startup, reset, maintenance and communication availability with approved recovery order.
Acceptance: Restart host and guests independently in benign test; controller availability and session epochs follow allocated policy.

Requirement: The host-facing fleet telemetry interface shall export only approved data with controller identity, provenance, freshness and bounded buffering under the allocated data policy.
Acceptance: Host fixture verifies controller identity, actual installed/configuration identity where allocated, stale/unavailable quality, buffer pressure and out-of-scope export refusal. Reconcile delayed reports without inventing installed state; privacy follows ADOPT-029.

Requirement: Each selected Ethernet communication binding shall interoperate with an independent peer using its admitted protocol and network profile.
Acceptance: Independent protocol peer verifies supported normal exchange, version mismatch, link loss and recovery on the admitted configuration, including Ethernet edge where selected. Physical PHY evidence is governed separately by ADOPT-013/016.

Requirement: Integrated IPC shall invalidate stale session on peer restart.
Acceptance: Old intent rejected after peer reset.

Requirement: Integrated real-time targets shall define cross-domain ownership of devices, reset, clock, memory, boot images and DMA in a versioned processor-domain compatibility and initialization record.
Acceptance: Review SoC ownership, firmware dependency versions and initialization evidence; approved compatible sets work across independent restarts, incompatible sets fail admission or configuration is excluded.

Requirement: Zonal endpoint loss shall be contained to allocated domain.
Acceptance: Other benign endpoints remain within allocated resource limits.

Requirement: Selected CAN XL or FlexRay bindings shall preserve approved semantic contracts and physical network constraints.
Acceptance: Independent peer passes scoped protocol and availability fixtures.

Requirement: Selected PCIe, hardware mailbox or vendor IPC bindings shall preserve bounded communication, ownership and restart semantics.
Acceptance: Independent peer verifies approved contract, buffer ownership and restart behavior.

Requirement: Zonal traffic classes shall have explicit admission, bandwidth, latency and congestion disposition policies by interface and application.
Acceptance: Under approved competing traffic workload, allocated real-time classes meet timing while lower-priority drops are reported.

Requirement: Redundant network paths shall declare duplicate handling, path quality, recovery and delivery guarantees independent of application authority.
Acceptance: Benign test removes each path independently and restores it; duplicates and stale data handled per approved contract.

Requirement: Selected in-vehicle network protection shall use approved standard/provider mechanisms and explicit allocation of key lifecycle, latency and failure policy.
Acceptance: Independent conformance peer and timing assessment validate approved protected communication and defined unavailable-state behavior.

Requirement: Safety item assumptions and allocations shall be agreed before safety claims.
Acceptance: DIA, item scope, hazard and FTTI allocations approved as applicable.

Requirement: Mixed-criticality configurations shall demonstrate allocated freedom from interference and independence across timing, memory, DMA, accelerators and shared power/reset resources.
Acceptance: Independent analysis accepts evidence or excludes configuration.

Requirement: Cybersecurity risk and control allocation shall be traced.
Acceptance: TARA and control/residual-risk records approved by responsible integrator.

Requirement: Only approved authorized intents shall be admitted.
Acceptance: Denied roles and invalid domain requests do not change state.

Requirement: Device identity and credential lifecycle shall use approved security providers and hardware-backed storage where allocated, with explicit provider capabilities, credential ownership and regional policy.
Acceptance: Provisioning, authorized replacement, rotation, revocation and duplicate-identity refusal fixtures pass; review audit records and provider compatibility. Factory serial/test records are governed by ADOPT-009.

Requirement: Update admission shall verify authenticity, artifact identity, target hardware, configuration and dependent deployment-unit compatibility before activation.
Acceptance: Approved test artifacts cover valid and incompatible image/component/configuration combinations; unapproved authenticity, hardware, dependency or eligibility causes refusal. Physical trust and recovery follow ASR-026/007.

Requirement: Update recovery shall be validated for each admitted deployment-unit and storage/activation configuration, including flash and boot behavior when firmware activation is selected.
Acceptance: Interrupt approved activation at each allocated durable state boundary and restart the admitted configuration. Verify an approved compatible artifact, recoverable state or explicitly allocated unavailable disposition with actual identity reported; use physical flash/boot evidence when firmware activation is selected. State-schema compatibility follows ASR-030; model-specific recovery follows ADOPT-062.

Requirement: Each release shall state exact supported configurations, scope and limitations without unsupported production, interoperability, safety or security claims.
Acceptance: Reviewed statement reconciles PL-010 evidence, dependency limitations and accepted scope. Candidate, simulation, physical and independently qualified results are distinguishable; no unaccepted configuration or unsupported conformity claim is published.

Requirement: Safety analysis shall include reset, startup, update and shutdown states.
Acceptance: Allocated hazards and fault response across lifecycle covered.

Requirement: Safety communication protection shall have allocated fault model and residual error analysis.
Acceptance: Independent safety analysis and accepted assumptions recorded.

Requirement: Security review shall resolve debug lifecycle and safety/security recovery conflicts and consume approved supply-chain provenance evidence.
Acceptance: Debug and recovery policy plus joint risk acceptance documented; provenance traced to VER-003.

Requirement: Allocated silicon diagnostic mechanisms including ECC, hardware self-test and fault collection shall be integrated using approved vendor facilities and report validity.
Acceptance: Vendor assumptions and approved benign diagnostic fixtures verify reporting, readiness and allocated escalation.

Requirement: Allocated external safety PMIC and clock, voltage and thermal monitors shall report valid status and retain independent protection responsibilities.
Acceptance: Reviewed ownership and approved bench status fixtures demonstrate allocated behavior without replacing hardware protection.

Requirement: Cryptographic provider interfaces shall support controlled algorithm and key-format migration without changing application logic or silently weakening approved security policy.
Acceptance: Two approved provider configurations demonstrate compatible migration and refusal of unsupported or policy-disallowed algorithms. For selected long-lived/PQC scopes, review threat horizon, approved algorithms and measured target resource costs; unsupported providers stay open.

Requirement: Update policy shall distinguish artifact release version, compatibility version and applicable anti-rollback security epoch, permitting only explicitly approved recovery paths.
Acceptance: For each admitted artifact class, review independent release, interface/state compatibility and security-epoch fields and exercise compatible activation, incompatible target, policy-refused rollback and authorized recovery with approved test artifacts. An inapplicable security epoch requires approved rationale. Physical trust-chain evidence follows ASR-026 where selected.

Requirement: Released software inventory shall associate component versions and configuration fingerprints with the exact controller and authorized deployment record.
Acceptance: Reconcile controller identity, installed component, image, configuration and selected model fingerprints to authorized deployment and resolved build records at manufacture/service and before/after update. Missing or inconsistent values carry explicit provenance and disposition; never substitute desired for observed version.

Requirement: A selected verified-boot configuration shall admit executable images only through the approved target trust-chain policy.
Acceptance: Approved physical target and signed test artifacts demonstrate admitted image boot and refusal of unapproved image; recovery state and hardware trust assumptions are documented. Update admission remains ASR-006.

Requirement: A selected service replacement or decommissioning workflow shall enforce the approved disposition of retained product data, credentials and identity bindings.
Acceptance: Benign replacement and retirement fixtures verify revoked identity or authorized transfer, policy-defined data retention/deletion, and traceable disposition; unavailable hardware methods are recorded open.

Requirement: Each allocated safety fault reaction shall meet its product-defined detection-to-response time budget derived from the agreed fault tolerant time interval.
Acceptance: Approved benign representative fault fixtures measure detection and reaction against allocated timing, including reset and degraded modes; independent reviewer accepts analysis and physical evidence or excludes scope.

Requirement: Each allocated requirement shall trace bidirectionally from its stakeholder need or system objective through design and implementation or responsibility allocation to verification evidence.
Acceptance: Audit every applicable stable ID against a documented need/rationale, objective, design allocation, implementation or external owner and verification record. Orphans, missing links and unsupported acceptance block closure; derived records match Z12 under VER-008.

Requirement: Build shall pin toolchain and upstream inputs.
Acceptance: Immutable manifest, hashes and reproducible result recorded.

Requirement: Release evidence shall contain a verifiable artifact identity and build provenance, SBOM, dependency license obligations and applicable support/upgrade policy.
Acceptance: Independent verifier validates artifact authenticity and manifest correspondence, rejects mismatched artifacts, and reconciles resolved dependency inventory with license/provenance approvals. Hardware and independent qualification evidence remain separate.

Requirement: Test reports shall record exact configuration and raw observations.
Acceptance: Procedure, expected/actual, verdict, reviewer and identity present.

Requirement: Simulation claims shall state model limitations and physical correlation needs.
Acceptance: Model scope and differential plan complete; virtual execution does not imply physical qualification.

Requirement: Evidence gate shall reject missing required verification.
Acceptance: Missing or failed required evidence blocks release.

Requirement: Interface changes shall trigger compatibility and regression assessment.
Acceptance: Version decision and affected fixtures recorded.

Requirement: Each Z12 requirement record shall have a unique stable identifier and populated objective, applicability, normative statement, design reference, verification ID, method, acceptance criteria, gate, owner, status and evidence fields; derived registers shall match canonical fields.
Acceptance: Automated trace checks reject missing or duplicate identifiers, missing mandatory fields, unknown objective or gate and inconsistent canonical fields. Human review confirms one primary obligation, necessity, feasibility, semantic overlap disposition and acceptance consistency before baseline approval; need trace is governed by VER-001.

Requirement: Measurement procedure shall state timing source, uncertainty, conditions and sample scope.
Acceptance: Acceptance procedure and actual traces are reproducible; no measured maximum claimed as WCET.

Requirement: The project shall review coding-standard applicability, static analysis findings, compiler diagnostics and deviations for each supported release.
Acceptance: Approved C coding rules and deviation register reconcile with actual analysis results and build flags.

Requirement: Each applicable software requirement shall have positive, negative and boundary verification or an approved documented rationale why a category is inapplicable.
Acceptance: Evidence gate detects missing required test category; reports link each test and exact configuration to its acceptance criterion.

Requirement: Verification shall track structural coverage at the level required by allocated assurance scope, including justified unreachable code and reviewed exclusions.
Acceptance: Independent coverage report reconciles build identity, test execution and exclusions; unreviewed deficits block selected gate.

Requirement: Selected FMI or equivalent co-simulation interface shall expose versioned inputs, outputs, time-step semantics and model limitations.
Acceptance: Independent simulator executes benign reference scenario and compares outputs against native simulation within declared tolerance.

Requirement: CI shall build and verify every admitted release configuration and an approved coverage set for supported feature interactions using pinned inputs, with applicable regression and resource budgets enforced.
Acceptance: CI evidence lists all admitted release configurations, positive and rejected combinations and rationale for feature-interaction coverage; unsupported combinations are not claimed. Controlled build, regression and budget failures fail their gate and identify affected configuration. Physical evidence remains separate.

Requirement: Competitive benchmarks shall compare equivalent functionality, workload, operating conditions and assurance scope against a legally accessible baseline using a predefined comparison protocol.
Acceptance: For software-only metrics use matched hardware, compiler and instrumentation or disclose justified differences. For system/BOM metrics compare equivalent allocated functionality on explicitly identified complete architectures, including migration and qualification costs. Publish scope, test inputs, uncertainty, failures and unavailable baseline data; no unsupported superiority claim.

Requirement: AI-generated software, tests and engineering artifacts shall follow the same traceability, provenance, accountable review and verification controls as human-authored artifacts.
Acceptance: Sample changes show accountable reviewer, test identity and trace; automated evidence gate rejects an unrun test represented as passed.

Requirement: A requirement or architecture change shall trigger trace-based impact assessment on affected design, code, tests, configurations and previously accepted evidence before release.
Acceptance: Controlled requirement change identifies downstream and upstream links, invalidates affected evidence until re-verification and preserves unchanged evidence identity. Missing links block baseline acceptance.

Requirement: Each acceptance verdict shall identify the accountable reviewer and the independence required by its allocated assurance scope.
Acceptance: Sample verdicts reconcile reviewer, evidence identity, scope and required independence. Missing or conflicted review cannot satisfy the affected gate.

Requirement: Requirement applicability shall be derived from the approved deployment and capability manifest using versioned, unambiguous selection rules, rather than independent per-requirement toggles.
Acceptance: For every Z12 ID, produce applicable, not applicable with reviewed rationale, or unresolved with owner. Test standalone, legacy distributed, zonal, companion, integrated and AI-enabled/disabled cases; unknown predicates, inconsistent aliases, missing implied dependencies or unresolved mandatory allocations block the affected admission. Portfolio obligations are tracked separately from image requirements and cannot be waived by an image flag.

Requirement: Supplier contributions shall declare owner, interface, limitations and evidence.
Acceptance: Onboarding submission passes published checklist.

Requirement: Supplier-facing claims shall be restricted to exact configurations admitted under PL-010.
Acceptance: Published partner claims agree with authoritative target maturity data.

Requirement: Platform releases shall publish maintenance ownership, support duration, patch and response policy, API deprecation, dependency end-of-life and migration route.
Acceptance: Publish support dates, supported configurations, owners, response/backport policy, dependency EOL, migration route, archived build inputs and funding assumptions. Independently rebuild an admitted historical release and exercise a supported transition under ADOPT-038; longer commitments require agreement.

Requirement: Supplier admission shall allocate upstream maintenance and change-impact responsibilities.
Acceptance: Approved dependency and upstream maintenance responsibility record.

Requirement: Selected migration tooling shall translate legally authorized legacy signal, component-interface or diagnostic descriptions into validated native configuration without silent semantic loss.
Acceptance: Use pinned synthetic or licensed fixtures, e.g. DBC, LDF, authorized ARXML or diagnostic descriptions for the selected format. Compare supported identifiers, types, units, scaling, directions, initial/invalid values and versions to expected output; ambiguous or unsupported mappings are explicitly reported and block unattended admission. Rights and version limitations recorded.

Requirement: Supplier deliverables shall support explicit licensing boundaries, isolated proprietary application components and customer-specific configuration without mandatory core forks.
Acceptance: Independent integration builds two customer variants from common core without unrelated component changes. Verify licenses, separately controlled application inputs, absence of cross-customer data and traceability to customer acceptance under SUP-017.

Requirement: Selected engineering exchange interfaces shall preserve stable requirement, configuration, test and evidence identifiers and trace links across versioned machine-readable formats.
Acceptance: Independent import/export round trip using the selected format (e.g. ReqIF where applicable) retains identifiers, links and verdicts; unsupported fields explicitly reported, no silent loss or uncontrolled change to canonical Z12.

Requirement: ZARC shall maintain a versioned industry and competitor capability comparison for declared scope against a legally accessible AUTOSAR Classic release, relevant alternatives and published OEM, supplier and semiconductor roadmaps.
Acceptance: Quarterly review public direction; annually and before major roadmap changes review capability equivalence and standards applicability. Record source/date/version, equivalent/partial/not applicable/open, owner, Z12 trace, evidence, migration limits and disposition. Confidential roadmaps unavailable explicitly; no unsupported endorsement or equivalence.

Requirement: The common ZARC core shall be available under its declared open-source license with source and reproducible build inputs, without mandatory ZARC-specific runtime royalties or proprietary core tooling.
Acceptance: Review core license and resolved dependencies; independent developer builds a supported reference from published source with documented accessible tooling. Any selected restricted vendor SDK, proprietary application or commercial support dependency has an explicit license and replacement/availability limitation. No blanket third-party royalty-free claim.

Requirement: The reference portfolio shall include a standalone automotive MCU, a resource-constrained general-purpose MCU and an eligible heterogeneous SoC; these are platform-level objectives, not per-image dependencies.
Acceptance: Run the common benign application against the three declared target classes with exact manifests, limitations, measured footprint and no-host operation for the standalone targets. A physical target class remains open until independently validated; an unavailable eligible SoC does not invalidate unrelated configuration-specific evidence. PL-006 governs vendor portability.

Requirement: ZARC shall provide typed sensor samples with units, calibration identity, timestamp and quality.
Acceptance: Physical analog, digital, encoder and environmental fixtures pass normal and disconnected cases.

Requirement: ZARC shall provide bounded semantic actuator services with independent feedback and allocated fallback.
Acceptance: Benign lamp, fan and servo fixtures demonstrate feedback and approved fallback.

Requirement: Target electrical integration shall specify voltage, current, transceiver, power integrity, environmental and board-level constraints, including 12 V/48 V domain boundaries, isolation and protection ownership where selected.
Acceptance: Reviewed hardware specification and appropriate current-limited bench evidence match declared electrical constraints, power budget and hardware protection assumptions. No high-voltage or production claim from simulation.

Requirement: Selected calibration records shall be versioned, range-validated, provenance-traced and activated atomically at approved lifecycle boundaries through authorized operations.
Acceptance: Golden records and invalid-range, incompatible-schema, stale-revision and interrupted-activation fixtures preserve last accepted configuration or report allocated unavailable state. Calibration interface authority remains SVC-014.

Requirement: Selected peripheral services shall use supported native interfaces, including GPIO, ADC, PWM, SPI, I2C, UART, capture, SENT or PSI5 where allocated.
Acceptance: Each advertised interface has independent physical conformance evidence.

Requirement: Selected smart switches, current sensing and power-domain feedback shall expose typed device status and allocated voltage, current, temperature and fault-quality measurements without replacing independent hardware protection.
Acceptance: Current-limited low-voltage load and approved fault-response fixtures validate feedback, unavailable states and allocated hardware protection ownership. Power sequencing is SVC-023.

Requirement: ZARC shall support allocated wake sources, sleep modes and wake reason reporting.
Acceptance: Physical current and wake latency meet product allocations.

Requirement: Factory provisioning and end-of-line interfaces shall produce a traceable unit record containing serial identity, exact firmware/configuration identity and required test outcomes with approved retention.
Acceptance: Repeatable benign factory fixture creates unit record; wrong version, duplicate serial or incomplete mandatory tests prevent acceptance; credential lifecycle follows ASR-005.

Requirement: Hardware lifecycle management shall track silicon errata, stepping, board revision, vendor safety documentation and component substitutions.
Acceptance: Reviewed change impact and regression evidence for selected revisions.

Requirement: Selected physical CAN and CAN FD bindings shall meet the admitted communication profile and report bus state and recovery disposition.
Acceptance: Independent physical peer passes approved frame sizes, nominal and allocated peak bus load, lost-link and approved recovery fixtures. Report unavailable state until approved recovery and no unsupported link claim.

Requirement: Selected LIN controller or responder binding shall meet its admitted role, frame and schedule profile.
Acceptance: Independent physical peer passes admitted schedule, frame, timeout and sleep/wake fixtures; unsupported schedule or role is rejected.

Requirement: Selected standard or automotive Ethernet PHY, including multi-gigabit variants where allocated, shall meet link and electrical configuration requirements.
Acceptance: Physical link, throughput and recovery evidence against approved configuration.

Requirement: ZARC shall expose synchronized time with uncertainty and loss-of-sync quality.
Acceptance: Independent clock comparison meets allocated accuracy and degraded policy.

Requirement: Selected time-sensitive network traffic management shall satisfy allocated bandwidth, latency, queue mapping, switching/offload and time-aware scheduling policies under valid and invalid synchronization.
Acceptance: Independent competing-traffic and switch/offload tests verify selected schedule, queue mapping and latency bounds; loss of synchronization triggers defined traffic disposition. Clock quality follows ADOPT-014.

Requirement: Selected 10BASE-T1S segments shall conform to the admitted physical and access configuration, including node identity, access scheme and supported coexistence constraints.
Acceptance: Independent physical multidrop segment verifies declared access, timing, node configuration and peer loss; unsupported PHY/access combination fails admission.

Requirement: Each selected automotive diagnostic integration shall expose an explicitly versioned service catalog with configured identifiers, diagnostic-code mappings and response semantics through authorized diagnostic services.
Acceptance: For selected UDS or other admitted protocol scope, independent approved tester verifies supported service/identifier catalog, diagnostic-code mapping, unsupported service and unavailable behavior. Where selected, an authorized ODX description or equivalent machine-readable tester input matches the catalog. Session, transport and event behavior remain independently verified.

Requirement: ZARC shall map approved diagnostic content into selected ASAM SOVD interface.
Acceptance: Independent client confirms discovery, records and availability semantics.

Requirement: Applicable vehicle signals shall have versioned COVESA VSS mappings with stable identifiers and declared schema-evolution compatibility.
Acceptance: Golden mappings preserve units, quality and authority; old/new schema fixtures explicitly report unsupported fields and refuse incompatible mappings without silent reinterpretation.

Requirement: ZARC shall provide documented service boundary to selected Eclipse S-CORE release.
Acceptance: Independent integration fixture passes selected service contract.

Requirement: Selected legacy interoperability shall preserve approved semantics and authority across AUTOSAR, OEM contracts and applicable J1939 or ISOBUS gateway profiles.
Acceptance: Independent legacy peer or gateway passes predeclared signal, event, diagnostic and authority mappings for each advertised profile, including CAN/CAN FD or LIN where allocated. J1939/ISOBUS claims require selected version, addressing and network role fixtures. Migration tooling follows SUP-006; no unlicensed specification reproduction.

Requirement: The platform reference portfolio shall demonstrate coexistence of distributed standalone ECUs and a selected scalable zonal or hybrid multi-controller topology.
Acceptance: Demonstrate autonomous standalone operation without a host; independent conventional CAN, CAN FD and LIN peer fixtures on selected physical reference targets; and a hybrid/zonal reference with at least four physical controllers and approved independent failure domains. These may be separate benches. Compare equivalent allocated typed behavior across placements; record actual protocols, topology, failure results and unvalidated scope. Missing physical interfaces remain OPEN; simulation cannot close the physical criterion.

Requirement: Perception integrations shall allocate raw camera/radar/LiDAR data to appropriate processing paths and restrict ZARC to approved supervision and control contracts.
Acceptance: Architecture and workload evidence show perception traffic does not violate allocated MCU budgets.

Requirement: Selected safety product packages shall provide a configuration-specific assurance argument linking assumptions of use, semiconductor safety-manual allocations, safety manual, allocated requirements, analyses and verification evidence.
Acceptance: Independent reviewer accepts exact-scope evidence and assumptions or excludes scope; unresolved findings prevent unsupported safety claims.

Requirement: ZARC shall define ISO 26262 work products, responsibilities, independence and safety-related configuration change-impact review for selected safety scopes.
Acceptance: Product-specific process audit accepts allocated work products; a controlled change exercise identifies affected software, hardware, timing and independence assumptions and blocks release pending required re-verification.

Requirement: The platform shall maintain ISO/SAE 21434-aligned lifecycle work products and allocated organizational responsibilities; risk allocation is governed by ASR-003.
Acceptance: Responsible integrator reviews lifecycle process and work products.

Requirement: For regulated products, ZARC shall provide configuration and software-update evidence supporting applicable vehicle obligations, including UN R155/R156 and ISO 24089 where selected.
Acceptance: Responsible vehicle program reviews compliance evidence mapping; no platform type approval claimed.

Requirement: Selected coordinated multi-controller updates shall follow an approved compatibility and activation plan that specifies dependency order, readiness, compatibility windows and disposition of offline or older nodes.
Acceptance: Benign multi-node fixtures cover mixed supported versions, dependency order, interrupted activation, offline node, failed health check and approved recovery or degradation. Report actual versions and compatibility per node; local recovery follows ASR-007.

Requirement: Selected personal or sensitive data collection shall enforce product-defined purpose, minimization, retention, access and deletion or anonymization policy.
Acceptance: Approved data inventory identifies purpose and accountable owner; out-of-scope samples excluded and expired records handled per reviewed jurisdictional policy. Host export follows HOST-014.

Requirement: For each intended product and target market, regulatory and standards applicability shall be assessed with explicit allocation between platform, component supplier and vehicle/system approval holder.
Acceptance: Qualified reviewer approves jurisdiction and sector applicability record including non-applicability rationales, AI/data obligations, safety and software lifecycle references, accountable owners, required evidence and open findings. No inherited platform type approval; ADOPT-027 governs vehicle-specific update evidence.

Requirement: The project shall maintain a published vulnerability disclosure and incident response process with component-level affected-version assessment, accountable remediation and disposition for relevant advisories.
Acceptance: Maintenance drill with synthetic advisories traces intake, affected releases, triage, notification and remediation decisions; required unresolved findings block the allocated gate.

Requirement: ZARC shall maintain Automotive SPICE aligned engineering work products and review evidence.
Acceptance: Independent process gap assessment and action register published.

Requirement: ZARC shall assess tool confidence and qualification needs for each safety-relevant toolchain.
Acceptance: Tool assessment and selected validation evidence approved.

Requirement: Dependency changes shall be reviewed against the approved dependency inventory and upgrade policy before release.
Acceptance: Change review verifies compatibility, support and license impact; inventory governed by VER-003.

Requirement: Each supported profile shall provide a pinned reproducible SDK and a documented workflow for creation, build, simulation, test and evidence export using native west/CMake tooling and offline caches where licensing permits.
Acceptance: Independent clean environments build and run sample with pinned inputs; reproduce declared artifacts or documented exceptions. Missing dependencies fail with actionable diagnostics; offline-cache scope and licenses recorded.

Requirement: Build-time configuration generation shall deterministically resolve versioned feature, calibration, product-policy and board-wiring inputs without requiring an embedded configuration interpreter.
Acceptance: Identical input fingerprints produce identical resolved artifacts; two variants differ only in allocated selections. Contradictory or invalid inputs fail admission with field-specific diagnostics; PL-005 and PL-009 govern separation/conflict rules.

Requirement: The SDK shall provide provider and service templates that preserve native Zephyr development and avoid generic core changes.
Acceptance: Independent developer adds benign service without modifying generic runtime.

Requirement: Supported API upgrades, including LTS patches, shall preserve declared compatibility and deprecation policy through regression fixtures on maintained application contracts.
Acceptance: Exercise supported patch and API upgrades; compatibility fixtures pass or documented breaking-version and remediation decisions are approved before release.

Requirement: ZARC shall publish contribution, review, API decision authority, conflict-of-interest management, ownership and succession processes.
Acceptance: Independent contribution and one exercised change decision follow documented workflow; single-maintainer dependencies explicitly identified and mitigation recorded.

Requirement: Supplier integration material shall provide a reproducible checklist, interface control document and evidence template.
Acceptance: Independent integrator reproduces selected reference deployment.

Requirement: ZARC shall provide extensible documentation glossary and translation process for Chinese and Korean partners.
Acceptance: Reviewed glossary and localized quickstart preserve technical meaning.

Requirement: ZARC shall publish comparable integration effort and lifecycle cost evidence for a declared reference workload and production horizon, using the comparison method in VER-017.
Acceptance: For equivalent workload, production horizon and volume, record licenses, loaded engineering effort, hardware/BOM, integration, validation and qualification, migration, manufacturing, maintenance/support and field cost assumptions where available. Evaluate proposed 30% platform effort and 25% net lifecycle-cost savings under VER-017; include sensitivity and missing/negative results. These are portfolio competitive targets, not achieved savings or universal ECU admission thresholds.

Requirement: The public support matrix shall be generated from the authoritative target maturity records defined by PL-010.
Acceptance: Generate public target records from approved PL-010 data for the exact scope. Compare every published record and capability verdict against its authoritative input, including unsupported, unknown, simulated and physically validated states. A missing record or evidence must not promote maturity; no unsupported entries or unreviewed qualification claims.

Requirement: The platform SDK shall include an independently reproducible staged migration and coexistence reference for an existing distributed ECU system.
Acceptance: An independent integrator uses lawful conventional ECU/peer fixtures, imports representative DBC and LDF descriptions and, where legally available, an authorized ARXML interface fixture under SUP-006. Incrementally replace a benign application and demonstrate equivalent allocated behavior, unchanged legacy peer behavior, isolated application/configuration and an approved fallback to original reference deployment. Report manual steps, engineering effort, missing format evidence and limitations; protocol fidelity follows ADOPT-021.

Requirement: ZARC shall publish reproducible low-voltage reference kits for a benign intelligent edge and zonal use case.
Acceptance: Independent reproduction verifies at least 50 configured representative signal contracts across the published reference kits. Enumerate physically exercised versus simulated channels separately; every claimed physical interface has an approved physical fixture. Publish BOM, wiring, manifests, measured footprint, integration effort and limitations; simulated channels cannot count as physically validated.

Requirement: ZARC shall connect actual controller telemetry to the selected vehicle visualization with provenance.
Acceptance: End-to-end fixture reconciles observed nodes/components to intended topology, reports missing/unexpected identities and distinguishes measured, simulated, stale and unavailable. The reference dashboard is observation-only.

Requirement: Selected virtual ECU tooling shall provide deterministic scenario execution with controlled time, recorded seed, event replay and explicit model limitations.
Acceptance: Repeat identical scenario and compare normalized observations; changed seed and model assumptions recorded; injected benign faults reproduce expected transitions. Physical correlation follows VER-005.

Requirement: ZARC shall publish per-profile boot, latency, jitter, RAM, flash, CPU and power measurements for an identified workload, including active, idle, sleep and wake behavior where applicable.
Acceptance: Reproduce measurements per profile and allocated component or shared domain for boot, latency distribution, worst observed latency, misses, jitter, RAM, flash, CPU and power with instrument overhead and uncertainty. Calibrated energy bench records energy/task and state residence; observed maximum is not WCET.

Requirement: Selected product stress verification shall measure sustained workload against approved endurance and resource allocations.
Acceptance: Approved-duration run and analysis meet documented bounds; storage-specific endurance governed by SVC-010.

Requirement: ZARC shall verify approved benign fault cases across startup, normal operation and shutdown.
Acceptance: Independent HIL report records expected and actual outcomes.

Requirement: ZARC shall publish requirement trace, failed tests, missing evidence and supported configuration status.
Acceptance: Compare published trace, test failures, missing evidence and supported configuration status against authoritative Z12 and approved configuration-specific verification records. Check an unrun, failed, blocked and accepted fixture; each remains distinguishable and missing evidence cannot be represented as accepted. Apply approved confidentiality and disclosure policies.

Requirement: ZARC shall provide repeatable SIL/HIL orchestration using versioned logical stimuli, target-specific fixture definitions, calibration and exact target identity.
Acceptance: Independent runner recreates selected virtual and physical reference tests; records raw observations, fixture calibration, test limits and deviations. A second admitted physical bench verifies portability of the fixture where selected.

Requirement: Each supported profile shall allocate measurable startup, RAM, flash, CPU, latency, jitter, energy and headroom budgets before admission, derived from its intended workload.
Acceptance: Budget manifest contains value, units, measurement method, workload, owner and approval for each applicable metric; CI flags size regression, physical evidence meets approved timing/power bounds, and unapproved or missing budgets block admission.

Requirement: Local or external advisory AI shall have no direct physical-resource authority; unavailable, expired or failed inference shall not prevent independently allocated deterministic function.
Acceptance: Benign predictive-maintenance or sensor-anomaly fixtures exercise local and/or external AI paths as admitted. Verify advisory-only interface, invalid/expired output, timeout, unavailable provider, overload and reset; independently allocated deterministic function remains within its timing and resource allocation. AI-disabled exclusion follows SYS-010; external advice provenance follows ADOPT-059; safety-related use requires ADOPT-069.

Requirement: Each model artifact shall carry immutable identity, input/output schema, preprocessing version, supported precision, runtime compatibility and provenance.
Acceptance: Model admission fixtures accept matched artifact and reject wrong shape, version, digest and unsupported operation.

Requirement: Each model shall declare peak working memory, persistent storage, execution deadline, energy envelope and concurrency limits for the exact target.
Acceptance: Measure approved workloads and worst observed behavior on target; reject allocation beyond profile budget and report uncertainty.

Requirement: AI input shall carry sample provenance, quality, units, age and preprocessing identity; missing or out-of-scope input shall produce explicit unavailable or low-confidence status.
Acceptance: Inject benign missing, stale, out-of-range and mismatched-preprocessing fixtures; output quality matches policy.

Requirement: Each admitted local or external AI output shall carry provider/model identity, timestamp, validity, confidence or applicable uncertainty metric, and advisory semantics.
Acceptance: Golden fixtures cover missing identity, low confidence, expired output, version mismatch and provider restart. Consumer marks unusable output per approved policy and never represents an advisory as confirmed physical state. Local runtime and external host allocation are recorded separately.

Requirement: Model deployment shall verify authenticity, runtime/schema compatibility and target resource admission separately from firmware version.
Acceptance: An approved signed test model is admitted only with matching runtime, schema, identity and resource allocation. Invalid authenticity, incompatible schema or budget overflow fails admission without making the proposed artifact active. Interruption and recovery are assessed under ADOPT-062.
